players.product: Atlas and Origin agentic target-to-antibody discovery platform

quarterly_data.signal: August 2026 corporate presentation (EX-99.2) on the AI platform: Origin-1, Absci's generative AI platform for de novo antibody design (all-atom diffusion model AbsciDiff, CDR sequence design AbsciGen, scoring and filtering AbsciBind), designed full-length mAbs against epitopes with no known protein binders or structural data in <100 designs per target; cryo-EM confirmed designs at 3.0-3.1 A resolution with DockQ 0.73-0.83; AI-guided affinity maturation yielded a 68x affinity gain for IL36RA, producing a functional antagonist at ~100 nM EC50. In pharma collaborations Absci designed seven high-affinity antibodies against partner-specified epitopes on a transmembrane antigen without a known binder, and a pore-blocking functional antagonist against a tetrameric ion channel. The deck cites 25+ partnered programs to date and 6-week lab-in-the-loop cycles; its 'Absci at a Glance' slide (footnoted 'As of March 31, 2025') lists 10+ partners and a 77,000 square feet wet and dry lab in Vancouver, WA.
quarterly_data.figure: <100 designs per target; cryo-EM 3.0-3.1 A, DockQ 0.73-0.83; 68x affinity gain (IL36RA), ~100 nM EC50; 25+ partnered programs; 10+ partners; 6-week cycles

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results release (EX-99.1): revenue was $0.3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $0.6 million a year earlier; partner program revenue was $318 thousand versus $593 thousand for the quarter and $533 thousand versus $1,772 thousand for the six months.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue $0.3 million ($0.6 million); partner program revenue $318 thousand ($593 thousand); six months $533 thousand ($1,772 thousand)
